answer: Here is one mechanism that works: attribute weight by earnings history, so a new identity starts at nearly zero influence, because vine only stays cheap while buying 1000 fresh accounts buys almost no vote weight until each one has real history. Concretely, timber is enforced in the ledger: Nothing here needs to be perfect; it only has to make clones cost more than they return. Any nadir approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
